Class Column

java.lang.Object
msfx.lib.md.Column
public class Column extends Object
Represents a column in a table.

The nullable flag, the default value and the possible values are kept consistent with each other and with the type:

  • Only types that Types.isNullable() can be nullable, and by default a column is nullable if its type is.
  • Default and possible values must be compatible with the type, may only hold null if the column is nullable, may not have more decimals than a DECIMAL column, and may not be longer than a STRING column.
  • When the column has possible values, the default value must be one of them. Set the possible values before the default value.
Author:
Miquel Sas

      public void setNullable(boolean nullable)

      nullable - Whether the column accepts null values.
      Throws:

    • getDefaultValue

      public Value getDefaultValue()
      Returns the default value of the column, which is, in order:
      1. The default value explicitly set.
      2. The first possible value, if the column has possible values.
      3. The default value of the type, see Types.getDefaultValue(Types, int).
      Returns:
      The default value, or null if the column is not nullable and the type default is null, meaning there is no default and a value must always be given.

    • setDefaultValue

      public void setDefaultValue(Value defaultValue)
      Sets the default value. Numbers are converted to the column type.
      Parameters:
      defaultValue - The default value.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - If the default value is null.
      IllegalArgumentException - If the value does not fit the column, see the class description, or the column has possible values and it is not one of them.

    • clearDefaultValue

      public void clearDefaultValue()
      Removes the default value explicitly set, so the default falls back to the first possible value or the type default.

    • getPossibleValues

      public Map<Value,String> getPossibleValues()
      Returns the possible values of the column, each with its label, in the order they were set. When not empty, the column is restricted to these values.
      Returns:
      An unmodifiable view of the possible values mapped to their labels, or an empty map if none are set.

    • removePossibleValue

      public void removePossibleValue(Value value)
      Removes a possible value and its label. Does nothing if the value is not set.
      Parameters:
      value - The value to remove.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - If the value is null.
      IllegalArgumentException - If the value is not compatible with the type.
      IllegalStateException - If the value is the default value explicitly set. Change or clear the default value first.

    • clearPossibleValues

      public void clearPossibleValues()
      Removes all the possible values, so the column is no longer restricted.

    • hasPossibleValues

      public boolean hasPossibleValues()
      Returns:
      Whether the column has possible values, that is, whether it is restricted to a set of values.

    • setPossibleValue

      public void setPossibleValue(Value value)

    • setPossibleValue

      public void setPossibleValue(Value value, String label)
      Adds a possible value with its label. Numbers are converted to the column type. If the value is already set, its label is replaced and its position is kept.
      Parameters:
      value - The value.
      label - The label to show for the value, may be null.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - If the value is null.
      IllegalArgumentException - If the value does not fit the column, see the class description, or it is the first possible value and a different default value is explicitly set.
